headline: Southern Cross Media sees advertising market recovery ahead but urges focus on controllable cost base amid ongoing uncertainty
reasoning: Rohan Lund notes that consumer and brand uncertainty is weighing on the advertising market but expects conditions to improve as confidence returns. He cautions against over-optimism on timing and says the company is focusing on controlling its cost base to withstand cyclical downturns. He also highlights that TV has been overcorrected against and expects that to normalize, which would benefit the business.
quote: I mean for brands, it's there's so much uncertainty, consumer uncertainty. And in any stability right now and any confidence coming back can only be good for us. I think the way we try to think through the business is, you know, I don't want to get overoptimistic and put times where I think that it bounces back. I've spoken to the group around. We have to be able to withstand those cycles. So let's focus on our cost base. Let's do what's controllable. So control the controllable. And one of that is digital. Because what we are seeing is quite a you know, you've got a big digital market of which we barely scratch. And you've got momentum in that digital market as well, which we should be capturing. So no, I it will return. And you know, but part of that's also going to be telling our story a little bit better because there's been an certainly an overcorrection against TV. And you know, and that will normalize over time.
episode_title: Southern Cross Media turns to "total TV" as ad market stays tough

headline: Southern Cross Media sees digital platforms as both a distribution opportunity and a monetisation challenge, pushing for fair payment from big tech
reasoning: Lund describes a dual perspective on global social media giants: while they represent headwinds through fragmentation, they also offer tailwinds as Southern Cross content — including over a billion monthly streams of Seven News — is consumed on TikTok, Meta and YouTube. He says the company needs to commercialise this reach through different content formats and new audience segments. He also signals an intent to push for fair payment from big tech and AI companies under the NBA legislation if commercial agreements are not reached.
quote: I use this language internally, the the headwinds of fragmentation and the rise of those giants. Let's look at it for the tailwinds that's also there. And that is that a lot of our content gets consumed on those platforms. Um, we see, you know, more than a billion streams of our seven news product is viewed every month across TikTok, meta, YouTube. Um, we've got to start commercializing that. We've got to start looking at our content assets and maybe different formats, thinking through sport, thinking through our shows that have another life and another audience segment to reach across those platforms. But we also look at those platforms in terms of, you know, fighting that they they pay fairly for what they take. You know, we invest substantial money in news across every town in this country, and it's an expensive product news to create, trusted news and to employ journalists as we do. And, you know, so we we want to work with those digital players to make sure they pay fairly. And if they're not, then we look to government to intervene and help. And that's the NBA legislation.
episode_title: Southern Cross Media turns to "total TV" as ad market stays tough

headline: Australian advertising market remains soft and volatile, with digital now representing $25 billion of a $30 billion total market
reasoning: Rohan Lund described the broader Australian advertising market as soft and volatile, with the total TV market down 9.9% in the prior year. He noted that the total advertising market is approximately $30 billion, of which $25 billion is now digital, highlighting the structural shift away from traditional broadcast. Southern Cross is seeking to capture a larger share of the digital market commensurate with the audiences it commands across its platforms.
quote: It's a $30 billion market in total, but 25 billion of that's digital. And so just thinking about our business and being more aggressive and a little bit bolder in, you know, taking our share the share that we deserve for the audiences that we have.
episode_title: Southern Cross Media turns to "total TV" as ad market stays tough

headline: Southern Cross CEO sees 'flight to trust' in publishing as digital circulation grows and misinformation drives audiences to mastheads
reasoning: Lund argued that trusted news mastheads are becoming more relevant in an age of misinformation, creating a structural tailwind for quality publishing brands. He noted that audiences are shifting to digital consumption — via apps and phone — rather than print, and Southern Cross is seeing strong growth in digital circulation. Assets like The Nightly are opening a more national footprint. The strategy mirrors audio and TV: prioritise total audience reach across digital and linear rather than defending the legacy format.
quote: What we have is an opportunity where, you know, there's a flight to trust. We're seeing mastheads become more relevant as people are looking for news. We're in an age of misinformation, so trusted news becomes more important. But how they want to consume that? For some people, that'll be through their phone, through their app. And it's making sure we have the same emphasis on our digital access to those audiences, rather than just thinking our business is about print.

headline: Southern Cross Media's audio division shows resilience with strong margins and growing digital listener momentum
reasoning: Lund expresses pride in the audio segment's performance in what he describes as a tough market last year, crediting the team's discipline on cost and margins. He highlights the role of digital and listener growth as drivers and expects this momentum to continue into the current year. He frames audio as a resilient category overall.
quote: Audio is such a resilient category. And for the business there you know John Kelly and the team did such a terrific job because they're they're ruthless on their margins. And you know they constantly looking at their cost base but also recognizing the role digital and listener plays in their growth. Now I'm very proud of the audio result. I think it stood up well in what was a pretty tough market last year, but for them to see that growth and I think we'll see that continue. I think they've you know, they've got the machine working well and I think we'll see more more momentum this year.

headline: Southern Cross Media CEO flags TV share gains and VOD growth as offsets to soft ad market following merger with Seven
reasoning: Southern Cross Media posted a 4.5% revenue decline to $1.87 billion in its first results post-merger, with net profit falling 57% to $9.9 million. However, the company delivered $30 million in merger synergies a year ahead of schedule. Despite the overall TV market being down 9.9%, SXL's TV revenue fell only 6.6%, reflecting share gains. VOD/streaming (Seven Plus) was up 50% year-on-year and accelerating, and the company is repositioning around a 'total television' strategy that treats digital as core, not peripheral. FY27 guidance shows TV revenue tracking flat in Q1, audio up low single digits, and publishing stable, though the ad market is described as soft and volatile.
quote: We we can definitely see you know, what we can't see is we have a very short and volatile market. We've had a good start to the year. We've actually seen growth year on year in in July. But that's just one month. But we're certainly seeing some better signs at the moment. But we understand the market is still down. So a lot of that is share growth. We're continuing to see for our business against peers in TV. And we're also seeing very strong growth in our digital business for TV. You know, the VOD business was up 50% year on year, but that's accelerating at the moment in terms of that, in that asset. And, you know, we think about total television.
episode_title: Southern Cross Media turns to "total TV" as ad market stays tough
